decisions.decision: Speculative decoding behind a measurement, with the tree sized to the batch rather than to a paper
decisions.instead_of: on by default at a published tree size, or off because the batch is large
decisions.because: at the fleet's batch of 60 a tree of 7 tokens is worth 3.13x -- speculation survives a large batch -- while the tree chosen at batch 1 is 0.23x, slower than not speculating at all; and whether it pays at all depends on an acceptance rate this traffic has never been measured for
decisions.would_change: the measurement that has not been made: the share of this service's replies that quote their prompt. Chapter 30 measured that number spanning 7% to 92% across four shapes of reply, which is the difference between worthwhile and pointless

decisions.decision: If it is on, draft from the prompt
decisions.instead_of: training and serving a draft head
decisions.because: three Medusa heads add 3.25 GB to a 16.0 GB model, 20.3% more weight read on every step, so the speedup starts 1.203x behind; drafting from the prompt adds nothing and returns 7.03x on input-grounded replies
decisions.would_change: traffic that is not grounded in its prompt: the same drafter returns 1.11x there, and a trained head is the only option left

decisions.decision: Constrain the structured endpoint, compiling each schema once at startup
decisions.instead_of: prompting for JSON and parsing defensively, or compiling per request
decisions.because: the mask costs 0.00010% of a decode step's traffic and the whole grammar compiles to 128 bytes, so the only real cost is the compile, which a fixed schema pays once
decisions.would_change: accepting arbitrary JSON Schema per request, which moves the compile onto the request path and into the first-token latency

decisions.decision: An exact-match response cache, keyed on every field the answer depends on
decisions.instead_of: no cache above the model, or a semantic one
decisions.because: an exact cache answers 77% of single-turn traffic with no wrong answers, while a similarity threshold set above the worst confusable pair still answers 40% of requests wrongly on traffic that carries account numbers
decisions.would_change: traffic with no repeated questions, where the cache is dead weight -- and agent traffic, where it already is

decisions.decision: No thinking budget on the default endpoint
decisions.instead_of: thinking on by default, as several providers now ship it
decisions.because: the case study promises a first token inside 1,000 ms and a reply in seconds; a reply behind 32,768 thinking tokens takes 479 s and costs 888 times as much
decisions.would_change: a second endpoint for work that is worth minutes and is asked for asynchronously, which is what the provider documentation recommends above a 32k budget

decisions.decision: A dense model, and a context ceiling well short of 128K
decisions.instead_of: a mixture of experts, or an unbounded context window
decisions.because: DeepSeek-V3's weights alone are 1,342 GB and need 17 accelerators before anything is served, against a fleet of 8; and a 128K context admits 3 sequences a machine
decisions.would_change: demand large enough to keep a mixture's fleet busy, where its cost per token is several times better -- this is a decision about scale, not about architecture

interaction.note: Chapter 30's speedups were measured at four batch sizes and interpolated between them, never past them
